measured.machine: AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX 16-Core (32 logical cores), 92 GiB RAM, Linux 7.0.0 x86_64, go1.26.0, gcc 13.3.0, opengrep 1.22.0
measured.method: Three runs of `budgets.sh all`; `measured` is the highest of the three. Each run takes the median of 11 runs for startup and of 5 runs (after one warm-up) for scan wall time, and the highest peak RSS of those 5. Spread across the three runs: size identical, startup 15/15/15 ms, deps_go 305/308/306 ms and 99964/99712/99532 KB, polyglot 401/399/400 ms and 113324/113192/113288 KB.

binary_size_bytes.why: Measured size plus 10%. Two builds of one tree match byte for byte; the CI runner's checkout and module-cache paths (no -trimpath in the release build) and a newer go1.26 patch move it by well under 1% (-trimpath alone saves 98656 bytes here). A breach means new code or a new dependency added over 4 MB: re-measure and raise it in the same PR only when that growth is intended.

startup_help_ms.why: CLI startup has no published threshold, so this is a loose limit: about 16 times the measured median, room for a slow shared CI runner, and still under a 300 ms stall at startup, which it must catch (planted with a sleep in main).

startup_version_ms.why: Same reasoning as startup_help_ms: `version` must not do more work at startup than `--help`.

scan_deps_go_wall_ms.why: Loose limit, about 10 times the measured median: a 4-core CI runner is several times slower than the measuring machine and opengrep start-up dominates. It catches a scan that starts hanging, retrying or re-resolving the dependency tree, not a 20% slowdown.

scan_deps_go_peak_rss_kb.why: Twice the highest measured peak. GC timing and the number of dependency workers (one per core) move it; doubling the working set on a 3-module fixture means a leak or an unbounded cache.

scan_polyglot_wall_ms.why: Loose limit, about 10 times the measured median, for the same reasons as scan_deps_go_wall_ms; this scan builds two call graphs (Java and TypeScript).

scan_polyglot_peak_rss_kb.why: About twice the highest measured peak, for the same reasons as scan_deps_go_peak_rss_kb.

ci_test_suite_seconds.note: Not a budget and not checked by budgets.sh: the duration of the `Run tests with coverage` step of the last 10 successful `Test & Coverage` runs on main (gh run list --workflow test.yml --branch main --status success, then the jobs API), measured 2026-11-02. Re-read it when CI feels slow.
